issue.title: Spurious warning in situation involving bytes, overload, lambda
issue.body:
Discovered as part of https://github.com/python/typeshed/pull/7679

Given the following:
```
from typing import Any, Callable, overload

@overload
def sublike(pattern: str, repl: Callable[[str], str]) -> str: ...
@overload
def sublike(pattern: bytes, repl: Callable[[bytes], str]) -> bytes: ...
def sublike(*args, **kwargs) -> Any: ...

def minv1() -> str:
    return sublike("asdf", lambda m: f"{m}")
```
mypy produces:
```
test.py:10: error: On Python 3 formatting "b'abc'" with "{}" produces "b'abc'", not "abc"; use "{!r}" if this is desired behavior
Found 1 error in 1 file (checked 1 source file)
```

If you change to `return sublike("asdf", reveal_type(lambda m: f"{m}"))`, you get:
```
asdf.py:10: note: Revealed type is "def (m: Any) -> builtins.str"
asdf.py:10: note: Revealed type is "def (builtins.str) -> builtins.str"
asdf.py:10: error: On Python 3 formatting "b'abc'" with "{}" produces "b'abc'", not "abc"; use "{!r}" if this is desired behavior
Found 1 error in 1 file (checked 1 source file)
```
So possibly related to the multipass logic for lambdas.

issue.title: errors: speedup for large error counts
issue.body:
We have a legacy codebase with many errors across many files
```
Found 7995 errors in 2218 files (checked 21364 source files)
```

For historical reasons, it hasn't been practical to fix all of
these yet, and we've been slowly chipping at them over time.

Profiling shows that `is_blockers` is the biggest single hotspot,
taking roughly 1min, and `total_errors` account for another 11s.

Instead of computing those values on read by iterating over all
errors, update auxiliary variables appropriately every time a
new error is recorded.

As part of this change, refactor the existing mechanisms to filter
out errors.

Instead of maintaining two separate mechanism to filter out errors 
boolean flag in `MessageBuilder` and explicit copy of `MessageBuilder`
or `Errors`), expand `ErrorWatcher` to support all relevant usage
patterns and update all usages accordingly.

This is both cleaner and more robust than the previous approach,
and should also offer a slight performance improvement by reducing
allocations.

issue.title: False positive involving `re.sub` and `+` operator introduced in mypy 0.960
issue.body:
### Bug Report

Consider the following snippet. (This is a minified example of the problem detected in https://github.com/matrix-org/synapse/issues/12996.)

```python
import re

"#" + re.sub(
    "PATTERN",
    lambda match: match.group(0) + "ANOTHER_STRING",
    "HAYSTACK",
)
```

[Mypy 0.950 is happy with this](https://mypy-play.net/?mypy=0.950&python=3.10&flags=verbose&gist=ba60332a802eac1d760e7901624da712), but [mypy 0.960 is not](https://mypy-play.net/?mypy=0.960&python=3.10&flags=verbose&gist=a40a88d26df2613541e6402694ecedf5).

> main.py:5: error: Unsupported operand types for + ("bytes" and "str")

AFAICS this is a legitimate usage of [re.sub](https://docs.python.org/3/library/re.html?highlight=re%20sub#re.sub), consistent with [the stubs defined in typeshed.](https://github.com/python/typeshed/blob/81fd55a885e678559471710f249c7e27d02ec212/stdlib/re.pyi#L135-L146)

### Additional

Strangely, removing either of the addition operators and the corresponding string literal causes mypy 0.960 to accept the snippet. That is, applying this change

```diff
- "#" + re.sub(
+ re.sub(
```
is [accepted](https://mypy-play.net/?mypy=0.960&python=3.10&flags=verbose&gist=d08e3a3c15cad6c0914ce947fb9226fc), and applying this change

```diff
-    lambda match: match.group(0) + "ANOTHER_STRING",
+    lambda match: match.group(0),
```
to the vanilla snippet above [is also accepted](https://mypy-play.net/?mypy=0.960&python=3.10&flags=verbose&gist=8285609da597ed67ef55105862f026e3).

I'm not sure how to get mypy to reveal the type of an expression in a lambda body, but I'd guess that in the error cases it deduces `match: Match[bytes]` rather than `match: Match[str]`?

body: This appears to have been fixed by a3abd3644c5f2c84d2fa65fb621327a6c6a0e695 (#12631), unless I did the `git bisect` wrong. I can't reproduce the error on the original example with a3abd3644c5f2c84d2fa65fb621327a6c6a0e695 checked out, but I can with the commit before it.

Hmm, this happened to me too with that exact same PR: https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/8814#issuecomment-1222759856 . Since it's unexpected, seems worth understanding the mechanism / adding regression tests.

Oh, looks like it's actually not _entirely_ unexpected: Jelle mentioned in https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/12631#discussion_r857181069 that the PR was touching logic that impacted this bug. But we should definitely add a test, agreed.

I'm getting the same error `mypy_test.py:6: error: On Python 3 formatting "b'abc'" with "{}" produces "b'abc'", not "abc"; use "{!r}" if this is desired behavior  [str-bytes-safe]` with the following repro

```
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({'A': [1]})

x = f"Hello {df.loc[0, 'A']}"
```

mypy: 1.0.0 (strict=True)
Sorry, ignore my previous comment, it went away when I upgraded `pandas-stubs`
This appears to have been fixed in mypy 0.960.

issue.title: Add regression test for fixed bug involving bytes formatting
issue.body: Adds a regression test for #12665, which is a strange bug that was fixed somewhat by accident

body:
We were keeping this open so that we didn't forget to add a regression test, since this was a strange bug that was fixed somewhat by accident: https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/12665#issuecomment-1324156230. But it looks like we forgot to anyway :)

I filed https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/15867 to add a regression test.
